newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sentences four to prison for March hijacking.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sentences four to prison for March hijacking.

text.p: An Egyptian state security court on Monday sentenced an Egyptian man to life imprisonment and three others to between three and 10 years in jail for hijacking a passenger plane from Egypt to Libya last March.
Three of the men, armed with petrol bombs and gunpowder, forced an EgyptAir Airbus 320 to fly to Libya, saying they had a message for world leaders on the plight of the Palestinian people.

They surrendered five hours later to Libyan security forces and all 140 passengers -- mainly Canadians, Japanese, French and Egyptians -- were freed unharmed. The hijackers were later extradited to Egypt.
Mohamed Mahmoud Hemid Selim, 43, got a life sentence, his son Khaled Mohamed Mahmoud Hemid, 17, was sent to jail for 10 years, and Ahmed Hussein Kamel Selim was given three years.
Abdel-Wahab Mukhtar Said, charged with supplying them with explosives, was sentenced to seven years in prison.
The four men said they wanted to draw the attention of the Egyptian government and world leaders to Israeli pressures on Palestinians.
